entries.flow:
Resolve use-case policy/current scope → classify allowed inputs → reserve budget atomically → load authorized source revisions → construct bounded native SDK request → validate structured output and source citations → mark ready or needs_review → reconcile actual usage. An official adapter existing for a provider does not prove a model supports JSON schemas, tools, embeddings or streaming in the chosen combination. School safeguarding, admissions, HR, finance and medical-like data require domain-specific review policies. Extraction can prepare a draft and evidence; it must not autonomously approve payment, alter student status or disclose another tenant's document. Model output is untrusted input that passes the same validation and authorization as a human request.

entries.name: Audit
entries.summary: Archive canonical scoped evidence with verifiable integrity, external checkpoints, retention policies and truthful limits against privileged tampering.
entries.model: Typed contracts, owned persistence and configuration are preserved in SOURCE_REFERENCE.md, original sections 5–6. Adapt to the actual implementation; these are not applied migrations.
entries.flow:
Authenticate issuer/scope → validate canonical envelope and redaction → same-store sequence/hash append → return receipt → background signer creates deterministic checkpoint → independently anchor/store under configured retention. Verify recomputes each entry and chain and checks signed/anchored head; a local chain alone cannot prove a truncated tail never existed. Export carries exact canonical bytes and public key references. Retention deletion needs current hold checks and storage capability acknowledgement; failed deletion remains pending, not falsely purged.

### Threat model must appear in README
A malicious database administrator with access only to the SQL store may alter a local chain; an independent signed checkpoint can expose that. An administrator who also controls signer keys and anchor storage may forge a replacement history. State which role controls each component and the evidence latency. WORM object storage, external time-stamping and legal requirements are separate capabilities with their own verification, not automatic consequences of using SHA-256.
entries.boundary: No claim of statutory certification, absolute immutability against an administrator controlling store+keys+anchors, legal advice, raw secret archive or replacement for source transactional audit records.
entries.infrastructure: SQL append store plus verifiable export; explicitly label as tamper-evident only against the defined attacker. Optional expanded profile: Independent signer/anchor, object-lock retention and separable roles for ingest, retention administration and verification.

entries.model: Typed contracts, owned persistence and configuration are preserved in SOURCE_REFERENCE.md, original sections 5–6. Adapt to the actual implementation; these are not applied migrations.
entries.flow:
Authorize plan → acquire source consistency mechanism → produce snapshot in staging → hash/encrypt/upload → publish immutable manifest → verify repository integrity → restore to isolated target → run database/application checks → label restore-verified. Multi-database plans either coordinate a host quiescence boundary/checkpoint or clearly record separate snapshot times; no false atomicity. Go build caches, npm caches, temporary development checkouts and PostgreSQL data directories are not interchangeable. This package backs up explicit application data; it must never classify arbitrary developer folders as obsolete or clean them to free disk. entries.name: Billing
entries.summary: Provide provider-independent commercial billing with exact money arithmetic, durable payment evidence and idempotent settlement while leaving accounting/tax law to explicit adapters.
entries.model: Typed contracts, owned persistence and configuration are preserved in SOURCE_REFERENCE.md, original sections 5–6. Adapt to the actual implementation; these are not applied migrations.
entries.flow:
Create draft with exact totals → finalize by CAS and freeze lines → persist payment intent/idempotency key → hosted checkout/provider request → verified callback or server reconcile → compare expected account/invoice/customer/currency/amount → settle payment, invoice/receipt and domain outbox together in the declared store. Domain order/entitlement consumers deduplicate by settlement ID and expose pending reconciliation when in other databases. Refund/reversal is a new audited state transition with entitlement compensation rules; it does not erase the original charge. Provider timeout after request is uncertain until verified.

### Payment and legal boundaries
Hosted checkout must keep PAN/CVV out of the host package and logs. Tax, invoice numbering, credit rules and retention vary by jurisdiction and legal entity; the host chooses a policy/adapter and obtains jurisdiction-specific review. Do not label this package ISO-, PCI- or tax-certified because its tests pass. The XOF example is a synthetic consumer example, not a statement that a particular merchant account can process it.

### Same-store versus distributed settlement
When the host order and billing records genuinely share one native transaction, provide a typed transaction participant. When they do not, emit a durable settlement event and wait for an entitlement/order receipt. The UI must distinguish payment verified from fulfillment complete. Retrying fulfillment must not repeat the provider charge.
entries.boundary: Not a general ledger, tax compliance engine, payroll, banking reconciliation product, PCI certification, storage for card PAN/CVV or guaranteed support in every merchant country.

entries.name: Licensing
entries.summary: Verify signed commercial entitlements, coordinate optional online activation and support explicit bounded offline operation without penalizing the free foundation.
entries.model: Typed contracts, owned persistence and configuration are preserved in SOURCE_REFERENCE.md, original sections 5–6. Adapt to the actual implementation; these are not applied migrations.
entries.flow:
Decode bounded envelope → enforce fixed schema/algorithm → select pinned trusted key by key ID → verify exact signed canonical bytes → validate issuer/audience/device/time/capacity → return typed status. Entitled checks the verified status and signed grants, never a UI flag. Activation persists request identity before network call; timeout after remote acceptance is uncertain and must reconcile using the same key. Expiry restricts paid actions with a clear message while preserving reading/export/backup policy and all free features.

### Operational truth
A user controlling the operating system can modify application code, restore old disks and alter clocks. A local verifier can validate a signature and apply a policy; it cannot provide absolute DRM or instantaneous offline revocation. A signed bounded offline lease and server-side benefits are the practical controls. Never store an issuer secret in Wails resources, obfuscated JavaScript or a Go binary.

### Commercial boundaries
Billing reports payment/subscription facts. A trusted licensing issuer converts those facts to grants. Features controls rollout; Defender still authorizes the actor. Paid module availability is the intersection of these decisions. A grace period and access to existing data must be documented per feature, not hard-coded as delete-all or deny-login.
entries.boundary: No home-grown cryptography, global offline seat-count guarantee, anti-piracy certainty, permanent fingerprint of a physical machine, payment processing, hidden telemetry or disabling free/local backups when a paid license expires.
entries.infrastructure: Free base mode plus offline verifier with pinned public keys; no network call needed for unlicensed/free features. Optional expanded profile: Activation service adapter, renewable signed leases, fleet/seat operations, key rotation and managed subscription entitlements.

entries.name: Modules
entries.summary: Provide deterministic, statically compiled Goravel modules with dependency validation, explicit operational lifecycle, and safe tenant-specific availability.
entries.model: Typed contracts, owned persistence and configuration are preserved in SOURCE_REFERENCE.md, original sections 5–6. Adapt to the actual implementation; these are not applied migrations.
entries.flow:
Manifest planning is pure: validate IDs/ranges → verify registry imports exist → calculate the graph → produce a stable digest. Generated `bootstrap/modules.go` contains explicit imports and provider values; the host wires this list into its provider registration before boot. No request reloads providers.

Lifecycle writes use compare-and-swap (CAS) revision checks and a durable operation ID. `requested → planned → migrating → ready → enabled`; failure records its last completed step and leaves availability false. Cross-database migrations are a saga, not one transaction: record each target receipt and resume idempotently. Disable first closes admission, then drains owned jobs, and only then records disabled; existing effects are not undone. Queued work carries module generation and must be re-admitted when executed. A disabled module retains its tables unless a separate destructive uninstall is approved.

### Host module layout (not the package repository itself)
```text
modules/admissions/
  module.json
  service_provider.go
  app/contracts/  app/models/  app/actions/  app/queries/  app/services/
  app/http/controllers/  app/http/requests/  app/http/middleware/
  database/migrations/  database/seeders/  database/factories/
  config/  routes/web.go  routes/api.go
  resources/views/  resources/js/  resources/lang/
  tests/unit/  tests/feature/
bootstrap/modules.go
```
Use the host's root `go.mod` initially. Module packages use deterministic Go import paths under it; generated imports are updated explicitly. A packaged third-party module can be a separate Go dependency but still registers compiled providers. An installable archive that changes Go code requires rebuild/redeployment: document this plainly for desktop and server hosts.

### Manifest security and upgrades
Reject arbitrary shell install scripts in manifests. Accept an explicit schema version, ID pattern `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,62}$`, semantic version and declared dependency ranges. Cap external assets and prevent zip-slip when an optional distribution tool is later introduced. The graph digest includes manifest bytes and selected dependency versions, not secrets. Never let a tenant administrator choose a Go import path. Adopt expand/contract database upgrades; destructive down migrations require operator approval and a tested backup.

### Standard examples
Provide a two-module inventory application plus a school admissions/learning pair. Examples must show a normal provider registration, module routes and a service call without requiring Admin. The paid-feature example injects a fake entitlement verifier explicitly marked test-only, plus a real signed-license adapter in a separate integration test when licensing exists. A boolean UI switch is never proof that an entitlement is valid.

Optional expanded profile: Optional persistent scope state, audited lifecycle commands, staged deployments, compatibility planning and Admin integration. entries.summary: Offer a portable scoped search API with native database backends and optional search-engine adapters while keeping authorization authoritative.

Query resolves authoritative scope before backend call, validates allowed filters and ranking options, then hydrates accessible hits. entries.flow:
Resolve current trusted scope → choose only the layers permitted by the key definition → honor a locked deployment value → validate decoded value → return an immutable copy with source and revision. Mutations address one explicit target layer authorized for the current actor, never whichever layer happened to win Get. A school reporting-period preference is a setting. Whether the reporting module is available is a feature/entitlement decision. Whether a teacher may read a student is authorization. ### Schema upgrades
Each definition has a schema version, migration ID and validator. A rename is a recorded move with conflict detection, not delete-then-create outside a transaction. A type change must specify transformation and a report of values that cannot be converted. Preserve old readers through an expand/contract window when required; never silently cast an arbitrary string to true.

entries.name: Sync
entries.summary: Synchronize selected domain data and offline commands between a local Goravel application and an authoritative server with explicit conflicts, revocation and resumable checkpoints.
entries.model: Typed contracts, owned persistence and configuration are preserved in SOURCE_REFERENCE.md, original sections 5–6. Adapt to the actual implementation; these are not applied migrations.
entries.flow:
Local domain transaction stores allowed command/outbox → send authenticated batch with device ID → server resolves current tenant/organisation access → deduplicate mutation/digest → check base revision and domain rules → commit business change+receipt+change log → return applied/conflict/denied. Pull captures an authoritative high-water mark and returns bounded changes up to it with signed scoped cursor. Client applies page and checkpoint in one local transaction. If access changes or tombstone horizon is exceeded, require a controlled resync and purge denied cache according to documented device policy. Remote revocation cannot retract data already copied to an offline device.

### Clear authority model
One machine can be a complete standalone application. Once a scope opts into synchronization, exactly one designated server is authoritative for that scope's accepted domain changes. Optional peer convenience cannot silently create two masters. A school's finance and central-admin PCs receive only authorized collections. Not all data must replicate to every device.

### Fundamental offline limit
A revoked user with an offline copy can still possess already delivered bytes. The system can stop future server access and request purge on reconnect; it cannot honestly promise instant remote erasure without an independently managed device/control system. Encryption and short offline leases reduce exposure but do not change that fact.
entries.boundary: Not database placement transfer, general PostgreSQL/SQLite replication, arbitrary model syncing, universal CRDT engine, file backup or permission to perform every online action offline.
entries.infrastructure: One-PC local authority mode works without any server; sync disabled until operator connects one. Optional expanded profile: Authoritative school server or managed cloud, selective device scopes, bounded offline commands and separate domain conflict handlers.

entries.flow:
Compile and publish immutable definition → Start commits instance and first intent → worker acquires fenced lease → revalidates instance state → executes handler with stable effect key → CAS records result and next intents. Approval evaluates current principal and instance scope at decision time, then records unique vote in one transaction; quorum transition is atomic. Timer processing creates a signal with deterministic fire ID. Cancel blocks new admission and optionally starts compensations; completed external work is not erased. ### First stable node set
Support task, decision, approval, wait-for-signal, timer, bounded parallel fan-out/join and terminal nodes. Decision expressions use a typed allowlisted AST, not a language interpreter. Every fork carries child IDs and a documented join rule; partial completion survives restart. Definition import is operator-controlled configuration, not permission for tenants to execute arbitrary handlers.

### Separation of duties
The workflow owner chooses whether requester and approver may be the same person, and whether delegated approvers count independently. Default finance sample requires a different current principal. Record principal, role/membership revision and policy decision reference, not a naked role string supplied by a browser.
